name: iot-device-management-system

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: An attacker could attempt to register unauthorized devices by intercepting the device registration process or compromising the certificate provisioning workflow.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker registers a malicious device using stolen or forged certificates, gaining access to send data into the system and potentially exfiltrate information about other devices.

recommendations.description: Implement strong device provisioning process with unique X.509 certificates
recommendations.implementationDetails: Use AWS IoT's just-in-time registration (JITR) with certificate-based authentication. Ensure certificates are securely generated and provisioned. Implement certificate rotation policies.
Implement whitelist-based device registration. Only allow authorized administrators to register new devices. Log and monitor all device registration attempts.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Configure IoT Core to use custom authentication, implement strict IoT policies, and enable detailed logging of device registration events. Use AWS IoT Device Defender to detect anomalies in device behavior.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: While the bucket has S3-managed encryption and public access blocking, IAM roles or bucket policies might grant excessive permissions to internal users or services.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An unauthorized internal user with overly permissive IAM permissions could access sensitive IoT data stored in the S3 bucket, leading to data breach.

recommendations.description: Implement strict S3 bucket policies and IAM roles
recommendations.implementationDetails: Review and restrict IAM roles, implement least privilege access, use bucket policies to enforce encryption in transit, and implement strict CORS policies.

recommendations.description: Enable advanced security features and monitoring
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable S3 versioning, MFA Delete, server access logging, and implement object lifecycle policies. Monitor access patterns using CloudTrail and CloudWatch.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using AWS KMS instead of S3-managed encryption for more control over key management. Implement S3 Object Lock for critical data. Use AWS Config rules to monitor bucket configuration.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Lack of comprehensive monitoring could allow attackers to perform malicious activities without detection.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker compromises a device or gains unauthorized access to AWS resources, and their activities go unnoticed due to insufficient monitoring.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable detailed logging across all services, set up alerts for security-related events, and implement automated response procedures for critical alerts.
Implement AWS IoT Device Defender for device monitoring, enable AWS GuardDuty for threat detection, and use AWS Security Hub for security posture management.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Enable AWS IoT logging with appropriate log levels. Use IoT Device Defender to monitor device behavior and detect anomalies. Implement automated remediation using AWS Lambda in response to security events.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Lambda functions with overly permissive IAM roles could be exploited to access or modify data they shouldn't have access to.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Processing Lambda to gain access to sensitive data in DynamoDB or modify device state information.

recommendations.description: Implement least privilege access for Lambda functions
recommendations.implementationDetails: Review and restrict IAM roles for each Lambda function. Implement resource-based policies where applicable. Use separate roles for different functions based on their specific needs.
Deploy Lambda functions in VPC when necessary, implement environment variable encryption, and use AWS Secrets Manager for sensitive values.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS SAM policy templates for secure Lambda role configuration. Implement function URL authorization if exposing Lambda functions directly. Consider using Lambda layers for shared security controls.

ground_truth.threatName: Denial of Service Through Message Flooding

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could flood the system with messages from compromised devices or through replay attacks.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: Multiple compromised devices send an excessive number of messages, overwhelming Kinesis streams and downstream processing capabilities.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure IoT Core message throttling, implement device-level rate limiting, and set up automatic scaling for Kinesis streams.
Set up CloudWatch alarms for abnormal message patterns, implement automated response procedures, and configure DynamoDB throttling protection.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS IoT Device Defender to detect abnormal message patterns. Configure appropriate Kinesis shard counts and implement error handling in Lambda functions for throttling scenarios.

ground_truth.threatName: Insufficient Access Control for Data Visualization

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Lack of proper access controls in QuickSight could allow users to view data from devices or organizations they shouldn't have access to.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An employee views sensitive IoT data from other departments or organizations through improperly configured QuickSight dashboards.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure row-level security in QuickSight based on user roles and organizations. Implement data source permissions and dashboard access controls.
Enable QuickSight audit logging, implement CloudWatch monitoring for data access patterns, and regularly review access logs.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use QuickSight's row-level security features with IAM for fine-grained access control. Consider implementing custom authentication solutions for QuickSight Enterprise edition.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""
AWS IoT Architecture Diagram
This script generates a comprehensive architecture diagram for a serverless IoT platform
using AWS services. The diagram illustrates the flow of data from IoT devices through
various AWS services for processing, storage, and visualization.

Author: Cline
Date: 2025-04-12
"""

# IoT & Edge Services
from diagrams.aws.iot import IotCore, IotAnalytics, IotRule
from diagrams.aws.iot import IotDeviceManagement, IotThingsGraph
from diagrams.aws.iot import IotGreengrass

# Compute & Serverless
from diagrams.aws.compute import Lambda
from diagrams.aws.integration import SNS

# Storage & Database
from diagrams.aws.database import Dynamodb, Timestream
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3

# Analytics & Monitoring
from diagrams.aws.analytics import KinesisDataStreams
from diagrams.aws.analytics import Quicksight
from diagrams.aws.management import Cloudwatch

# Security & Identity
from diagrams.aws.security import CertificateManager

# Core imports
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge
from diagrams.aws.general import Client, Users

# Custom styling
DIAGRAM_ATTRS = {
    "splines": "ortho",    # Use orthogonal lines for cleaner appearance
    "nodesep": "1.2",      # Increased spacing between nodes
    "ranksep": "1.5",      # Increased spacing between ranks
    "pad": "3.0"          # Increased padding around the diagram
}

# Edge colors for different types of flows
EDGE_COLORS = {
    "data": "#2673bf",     # Blue for data flow
    "auth": "#d94e4e",     # Red for authentication/security
    "mgmt": "#439c43",     # Green for management/control
    "monitor": "#a85cf0"   # Purple for monitoring/analytics
}

# Edge styling
def edge_attrs(label, color):
    return {
        "label": f"  {label}  ",
        "color": color,
        "fontsize": "12",
        "fontcolor": color,
        "penwidth": "2"
    }

# Node styling
NODE_ATTRS = {
    "fontsize": "13",      # Font size for labels
    "width": "1.5",        # Minimum width
    "height": "1.5",       # Minimum height
    "margin": "1",       # Margin around labels
    "imagescale": "true"   # Scale image to fit
}

# Cluster styling
CLUSTER_ATTRS = {
    "style": "rounded",
    "bgcolor": "transparent",
    "penwidth": "2",
    "fontsize": "14"
}

# Define the diagram
with Diagram(
    name="AWS IoT Serverless Architecture",
    filename="iot_architecture",
    direction="TB",      # Top to bottom layout
    show=False,         # Don't attempt to open the file
    graph_attr=DIAGRAM_ATTRS,
    outformat="png",
    node_attr=NODE_ATTRS
) as diag:
    
    # AWS Account boundary
    with Cluster("AWS Account", graph_attr=CLUSTER_ATTRS):
        # Private Security Zone
        with Cluster("Private Security Zone", graph_attr=CLUSTER_ATTRS):

            # IoT Devices and Users (outside AWS)
            devices = Client("IoT Devices")
            admins = Users("System Administrators")
            end_users = Users("End Users")

            # IoT Core and Device Management
            with Cluster("IoT Services", graph_attr=CLUSTER_ATTRS):
                iot_core = IotCore("IoT Core")
                device_mgmt = IotDeviceManagement("IoT Device\nManagement")
                cert_manager = CertificateManager("Certificate\nManager")
                rules_engine = IotRule("Rules Engine")

            # Data Ingestion and Processing
            with Cluster("Data Processing", graph_attr=CLUSTER_ATTRS):
                kinesis = KinesisDataStreams("Kinesis\nData Streams")
                with Cluster("Lambda Functions"):
                    process_lambda = Lambda("Processing\nFunction")
                    notify_lambda = Lambda("Notification\nFunction")
                    update_lambda = Lambda("Update\nFunction")

            # Storage Layer
            with Cluster("Data Storage", graph_attr=CLUSTER_ATTRS):
                timestream = Timestream("Timestream\nTime Series Data")
                dynamo = Dynamodb("DynamoDB\nDevice State & Metadata")
                s3 = S3("S3\nLong-term Storage")

            # Monitoring and Analytics
            with Cluster("Monitoring & Analytics", graph_attr=CLUSTER_ATTRS):
                cloudwatch = Cloudwatch("CloudWatch")
                quicksight = Quicksight("QuickSight\nDashboards")
                notifications = SNS("SNS\nNotifications")

    # Define connections with labels and styling
            # Device connections
            devices >> Edge(**edge_attrs("1. MQTT/HTTP", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> iot_core
            devices >> Edge(**edge_attrs("2. Register/Update", EDGE_COLORS["mgmt"])) >> device_mgmt

            # Authentication and security
            cert_manager >> Edge(**edge_attrs("3. X.509 Certs", EDGE_COLORS["auth"])) >> iot_core
            device_mgmt >> Edge(**edge_attrs("4. Device Identity", EDGE_COLORS["auth"])) >> dynamo

            # Data flow
            iot_core >> Edge(**edge_attrs("5. Route Messages", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> rules_engine
            rules_engine >> Edge(**edge_attrs("6. Ingest Data", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> kinesis
            kinesis >> Edge(**edge_attrs("7. Trigger", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> process_lambda

            # Lambda processing
            process_lambda >> Edge(**edge_attrs("8a. Store Time Series", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> timestream
            process_lambda >> Edge(**edge_attrs("8b. Archive", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> s3
            process_lambda >> Edge(**edge_attrs("8c. Update State", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> dynamo
            process_lambda >> Edge(**edge_attrs("8d. Trigger Events", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> notify_lambda
            notify_lambda >> Edge(**edge_attrs("9. Send Alerts", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> notifications

            # Device state updates
            update_lambda >> Edge(**edge_attrs("10a. Update State", EDGE_COLORS["mgmt"])) >> dynamo
            update_lambda >> Edge(**edge_attrs("10b. Deploy Updates", EDGE_COLORS["mgmt"])) >> device_mgmt

            # Monitoring and visualization
            cloudwatch << Edge(**edge_attrs("11. Metrics", EDGE_COLORS["monitor"])) << [iot_core, kinesis, process_lambda]
            quicksight >> Edge(**edge_attrs("12a. Query", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> timestream
            quicksight >> Edge(**edge_attrs("12b. Historical", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> s3

            # User access
            admins >> Edge(**edge_attrs("13. Manage", EDGE_COLORS["mgmt"])) >> device_mgmt
            end_users >> Edge(**edge_attrs("14. View", EDGE_COLORS["data"])) >> quicksight

"""
Architecture Notes:
1. IoT devices connect securely to AWS IoT Core using MQTT/HTTP protocols
2. Device authentication is managed through X.509 certificates
3. Device metadata and state information stored in DynamoDB
4. Real-time data ingestion through Kinesis Data Streams
5. Lambda functions process and transform data
6. Time series data stored in Timestream, long-term data in S3
7. Device state changes trigger notifications through SNS
8. System monitoring through CloudWatch
9. Data visualization through QuickSight dashboards
10. Administrators manage devices through IoT Device Management console
"""
